# Behavioral Design Specification: Entropy Source Core

## 1. Overview

The entropy source core is the central datapath and control block for generating entropy seeds from a physical random noise source. It accepts raw noise samples from an RNG input, subjects them to a set of health tests, optionally conditions the raw entropy using a cryptographic conditioner, and stores the resulting entropy seeds for delivery to either a hardware consumer or firmware.

The module must support the following high-level behaviors:

- Controlled enable and disable of entropy collection.
- FIPS-compliant and bypass operating modes.
- Boot-time phase behavior for lower-latency initial entropy.
- Continuous raw entropy sampling and packing.
- Multiple hardware health tests.
- An optional external health test interface.
- Firmware override and insertion of entropy data.
- A firmware-readable entropy output path.
- A hardware entropy output path with a FIPS-compliance flag.
- Interrupt and alert generation for operational and error conditions.
- Debug and status reporting.

All control and status behavior that is visible through the register interface must reflect the current internal state of the module and must be updated as entropy is collected, tested, conditioned, and forwarded.

---

## 2. Operating Modes

### 2.1 Disabled State

When the module is disabled, it must not:

- Enable the RNG source.
- Accept entropy samples for processing.
- Perform health tests.
- Generate entropy seeds.
- Assert entropy-valid or health-test-failed interrupts.
- Assert fatal or recoverable alert outputs, except for alert test requests or configuration/error conditions that are intentionally always monitored.

When the module is disabled, internal FIFOs and health-test counters must be cleared. The module must return to a known idle state.

### 2.2 FIPS-Compliant Mode

In FIPS-compliant mode, the module must:

- Use FIPS health-test windows and thresholds.
- Subject raw entropy to the full set of enabled health tests.
- Pass health-tested entropy through the cryptographic conditioner.
- Generate conditioned 384-bit entropy seeds.
- Mark delivered seeds as FIPS-compliant.
- Assert the FIPS-mode indication output to the RNG source so that the external RNG can operate under the appropriate generation requirements.

### 2.3 Bypass Mode

Bypass mode may be selected by configuration, or it may be used during the initial boot-time phase. In bypass mode, the module must:

- Use bypass health-test windows and thresholds.
- Pack raw, health-tested entropy directly into 384-bit seeds without cryptographic conditioning.
- Not mark delivered seeds as FIPS-compliant.
- Allow entropy to be consumed without additional conditioner latency.

### 2.4 Boot-Time Phase

After enable, the module may operate in an initial boot-time phase. During this phase:

- Entropy is generated using bypass-mode behavior.
- Health tests are still run, but with the bypass health-test window and thresholds.
- The resulting seeds are not FIPS-compliant.
- The module must complete this phase and then transition to normal operation based on the configured FIPS/bypass mode.

### 2.5 Mode Selection

The active mode is determined by configuration and, when applicable, by the current boot-time phase. The module must select the correct health-test window, threshold set, conditioner path, and FIPS flag based on the active mode. Software must be able to observe the current mode status.

---

## 3. Configuration and Register Access

### 3.1 Register Locking

The module must provide a register-lock mechanism. When locked, writes to control and configuration registers must be ignored. The register-lock state must be visible to software.

### 3.2 Secure Configuration Fields

Security-sensitive configuration fields must use secure multi-bit encodings. The module must treat invalid or unrecognized encodings as configuration errors. Invalid configuration must not enable the associated feature, and a recoverable alert/status must be set.

### 3.3 OTP/Fuse Gating

Certain features must be additionally gated by OTP/fuse enable inputs:

- Firmware read access to entropy data must be available only when the corresponding fuse enable is active.
- Firmware override control must be active only when the corresponding fuse enable is active.

If a fuse enable is not active, the associated feature must remain disabled regardless of register configuration.

### 3.4 Override and Insertion Control

Firmware override must become active only when:

- The fuse override enable is active, and
- The configuration selects firmware override mode.

In firmware override mode, the module must provide the following capabilities:

- A copy of post-health-test entropy must be written to an observe FIFO for firmware to read.
- A threshold may be configured in the observe FIFO depth. When the FIFO depth reaches or exceeds that threshold, an observe-FIFO-ready interrupt must be generated.
- If the observe FIFO overflows, it must stop accepting further data until it has been drained, and an overflow status must be reported.
- If firmware insertion is enabled, firmware must be able to write 32-bit words into the pre-conditioning datapath. A status must be provided when the insertion FIFO is full so that firmware does not overrun it.

Firmware-inserted data must be packed and must then follow the normal bypass/conditioning path selected by the current mode.

---

## 4. RNG Input

### 4.1 RNG Enable

The module must assert the RNG enable output only while entropy collection is enabled. When disabled, the RNG enable output must be deasserted.

### 4.2 Raw Entropy Sampling

The module must accept raw entropy samples from the RNG input whenever the RNG indicates that a valid sample is present and the module is enabled.

In normal operation, all bits of each RNG sample must be used for downstream processing.

### 4.3 Bit-Selection Mode

The module may be configured to test or use only one bit from each RNG sample. In this mode:

- The selected bit must be extracted from each incoming sample.
- The selected bits must be packed into the same bus width used by the normal datapath before being passed to health tests.
- A FIPS-compliant flag must not be asserted when bit-selection mode is active, because the resulting entropy stream is not the full-width RNG stream.

---

## 5. Internal Health Tests

The module must run health tests on the raw entropy stream before conditioning or forwarding. Each test may be independently enabled or disabled by configuration. When a test is disabled, it must not generate failure pulses or update its counters.

All health-test counters must be cleared when the module is disabled. A health-test clear condition must also be available to reset counters during operation.

The module must maintain separate threshold and window settings for FIPS mode and bypass mode. The active threshold and window must be selected based on the current operating mode.

### 5.1 Common Window Counter

A common health-test window counter must count valid entropy samples presented to the health-test block. When the counter reaches the selected health-test window size, the module must generate a window-wrap pulse for tests that operate on fixed windows.

The window-wrap pulse must be used by the adaptive proportion, bucket, Markov, and external health tests. The repetition count tests need not wait for a fixed window.

### 5.2 Repetition Count Test

The repetition count test must detect a stuck-at condition by counting consecutive repeated values on each RNG line. It must fail if a run of identical values exceeds the configured repetition-count threshold.

This test is continuous and must not be limited by the common window boundary.

### 5.3 Repetition Count Symbol Test

The module must also perform a symbol-level repetition count test. This test must detect repeated full-symbol values across the RNG bus. It must fail if any run of identical symbols exceeds the configured threshold.

### 5.4 Adaptive Proportion Test

The adaptive proportion test must monitor the proportion of ones in each window of raw entropy. It must have both high and low thresholds.

The module must support two threshold-scope configurations:

- Aggregate: thresholds are applied to the combined RNG stream.
- Per-line: thresholds are applied independently to each RNG line.

The test must generate a failure pulse if the measured proportion is outside the configured high or low threshold. It must also record the high and low watermarks observed during each window.

### 5.5 Bucket Test

The bucket test must count occurrences of each possible symbol within a window of raw entropy. It must fail if the count for any symbol exceeds the configured bucket threshold. This test is intended to detect symbol bias or inter-channel correlation.

### 5.6 Markov Test

The Markov test must detect unexpected first-order temporal correlations between consecutive entropy samples. It must track transition and non-transition counts, with separate high and low thresholds. It must fail if the measured value is outside the configured range.

As with the adaptive proportion test, the Markov test must support both aggregate and per-line threshold scope.

### 5.7 External Health Test Interface

The module must provide an external health-test interface with the following behavior:

- The current raw entropy sample and its validity must be presented to the external health-test block.
- A clear signal must be asserted when health-test counters should be cleared.
- The active enable signal for the external test must be presented.
- The selected high threshold, low threshold, and window size must be presented.
- The external block may return a generic count value, a high-failure pulse, and a low-failure pulse.

If the external block reports a failure, the module must treat it in the same way as an internal health-test failure for the purposes of:

- Setting the health-test failure latch.
- Incrementing external-test failure counters.
- Incrementing the aggregate failure counter.
- Generating health-test-failed interrupts and alerts.

### 5.8 Test Failure Counting and Alerting

Each health test must have its own failure count register. An aggregate failure counter must count any failure from any enabled internal or external health test.

The module must maintain per-test fail counters and a total aggregate fail counter. These counters must be visible to software.

When a health-test failure occurs, the module must:

- Latch the failure indication for the current window.
- Increment the relevant per-test failure counter.
- Increment the aggregate failure counter.
- Generate a health-test-failed interrupt if enabled.

If the aggregate failure count reaches the configured alert threshold, the module must assert a recoverable alert.

The alert-threshold configuration must be provided as a redundant pair. If the two fields are inconsistent, the module must:

- Not rely on the threshold.
- Report a recoverable configuration alert.

If the alert threshold is zero, alert generation from the aggregate failure counter must be disabled.

---

## 6. Entropy Conditioning

### 6.1 FIPS Path

In FIPS mode, health-tested raw entropy must be packed and fed into the conditioning block. The conditioner must produce 384-bit entropy seeds from the raw entropy stream.

The module must provide a halt request output to the downstream CSRNG/AES block while the conditioner is processing, so that power peaks are reduced. This request must be released when the conditioner operation is complete or no longer needed.

### 6.2 Bypass Path

In bypass mode, health-tested raw entropy must be packed directly into 384-bit seeds without passing through the cryptographic conditioner.

### 6.3 Final Entropy FIFO

All generated seeds, whether from the conditioner or the bypass path, must be placed into a final entropy FIFO. Each entry must consist of:

- The 384-bit entropy seed.
- A FIPS-compliance flag indicating whether the seed was generated in FIPS-compliant mode.

The final FIFO must have a parameterizable depth, with a default depth of 4 seeds.

If the final FIFO is full, new seeds must not be accepted into it. The module must continue operation in a way that does not corrupt the existing contents.

---

## 7. Entropy Output Paths

### 7.1 Hardware Output

The module must provide a hardware entropy output interface. When a hardware consumer requests entropy and a seed is available in the final FIFO, the module must:

- Pop the next seed from the final FIFO.
- Present the 384-bit seed on the output.
- Present the associated FIPS-compliance flag.
- Assert an acknowledge together with the seed.

If the final FIFO is empty, the module must not acknowledge the request until a seed becomes available.

The hardware output path must be disabled by default if software has routed entropy to the software path.

### 7.2 Software Output

The module must provide a firmware-readable entropy data path. Software access must be enabled only when:

- The fuse read-enable input is active.
- The entropy-data register enable configuration is active.
- The entropy route configuration selects the software path.

When software reads the entropy data register, the module must return the next 32-bit word from the software read packer and pop that word. A full 384-bit seed must be read as twelve 32-bit reads.

If no entropy word is available, or if software access is not enabled, the read must return zero and must not pop the FIFO.

The module must generate an entropy-valid interrupt when the software read path has at least one 32-bit word available.

---

## 8. Main Flow Control

### 8.1 Sequencing Behavior

The module must sequence the flow of entropy from the pre-conditioning stage to the final FIFO. It must only allow a seed to be written into the final FIFO when the correct source stage is ready and the mode-appropriate path has completed its processing.

The module must support a boot-phase indication. During the boot phase, it must prioritize lower-latency delivery of an initial seed. When the boot phase is complete, it must transition to normal operation.

### 8.2 Behavior on Health-Test Failure

If a health-test failure is detected for a window of entropy, the module must not forward the affected entropy as a valid FIPS-compliant seed unless the operating mode explicitly permits bypass operation. The module must record the failure, increment the failure counters, and generate the appropriate interrupt/alert.

### 8.3 Idle and Debug Status

The module must provide status outputs that indicate:

- Whether the main sequencing logic is idle.
- Whether the boot phase is complete.
- The current state of the main sequencing logic.
- The current depth of the final entropy FIFO.
- The conditioner status (e.g., absorbing, squeezing, block processing, errors).
- The current state of the acknowledge/handshake sequencing logic.

These status values must be visible through the register/debug interface.

---

## 9. Error Detection and Reporting

### 9.1 FIFO Errors

The module must detect the following error conditions for its internal synchronous FIFOs:

- A write attempted to a full FIFO.
- A read attempted from an empty FIFO.
- A FIFO reporting full while also being empty.

Each detected FIFO error must be reported in the error status registers. FIFO errors must be classified as fatal errors.

### 9.2 Counter Errors

The module must detect counter integrity faults in any redundant counter used for:

- Health-test windows.
- Per-test event counts.
- Per-test failure counts.
- Aggregate failure counts.
- Alert failure counts.

Counter integrity faults must be reported as fatal errors.

### 9.3 State Machine Errors

The module must detect illegal state transitions in its internal sequencing state machines, including the main flow-control state machine and the hardware-interface acknowledge state machine. Such errors must be reported as fatal errors.

### 9.4 Conditioner Errors

The module must detect errors reported by the cryptographic conditioner, including:

- Sparse state-machine errors.
- Counter errors.
- General conditioner error flags.

Conditioner errors must be reported as fatal errors.

### 9.5 Error Status Summary

The module must provide error status registers that indicate:

- Which FIFO generated an error.
- Which class of error occurred (write, read, or state).
- Whether an acknowledge state machine error occurred.
- Whether the main sequencing state machine error occurred.
- Whether a counter integrity error occurred.
- Whether the conditioner reported an error.

A fatal error interrupt must be generated when any fatal error class is active. A fatal alert must be asserted for the same set of conditions.

### 9.6 Diagnostic Error Forcing

The module must support a diagnostic capability that allows software to force the reporting of each error class. This forcing must affect the error status/interrupt path only; it must not corrupt the entropy datapath or FIFO contents.

---

## 10. Alerts

### 10.1 Recoverable Alerts

The module must assert a recoverable alert for the following conditions:

- Any security-sensitive configuration field has an invalid encoding.
- The main sequencing state machine raises a health-test-related alert.
- The entropy output bus-integrity check detects repeated data.
- The alert-threshold redundant configuration is inconsistent.
- The aggregate health-test failure count reaches the configured alert threshold.

### 10.2 Fatal Alerts

The module must assert a fatal alert when any fatal error condition is detected, including:

- FIFO protocol errors.
- Counter integrity errors.
- State machine errors.
- Conditioner errors.

The fatal alert output must be driven by the same error events that generate the fatal error interrupt.

### 10.3 Alert Test Capability

The module must provide alert test inputs. Writing a test request must cause the corresponding recoverable or fatal alert output to be asserted for test validation. Alert test requests must not change internal functional state.

---

## 11. Interrupts

The module must provide four interrupt outputs:

### 11.1 Entropy Valid Interrupt

Must be asserted when the software entropy read path has at least one 32-bit word available. This interrupt is cleared when software clears the corresponding interrupt status.

### 11.2 Health Test Failed Interrupt

Must be asserted when the health-test monitoring logic determines that a health-test failure condition requires software attention. This includes failures from internal health tests and from the external health-test interface.

### 11.3 Observe FIFO Ready Interrupt

Must be asserted when firmware override mode is active and the observe FIFO depth reaches or exceeds the configured threshold.

### 11.4 Fatal Error Interrupt

Must be asserted when any fatal error condition is detected, including FIFO errors, counter errors, state machine errors, and conditioner errors.

All interrupts must follow the standard enable/status/test behavior provided through the register interface.

---

## 12. Bus-Integrity Check

The module must monitor the entropy data delivered from the final FIFO for repeated values.

The check must compare a portion of the currently delivered seed against the portion captured from the previous delivered seed. If the two values match, and both values were validly captured, the module must:

- Flag a bus-integrity violation.
- Assert a recoverable alert.
- Report the condition in status registers.

The bus-integrity capture must be cleared when the module is disabled.

---

## 13. Reset Behavior

On reset:

- All FIFOs must be cleared.
- All counters, watermarks, and failure counts must be cleared.
- All state machines must return to idle.
- Interrupt outputs must be deasserted.
- Alert outputs must be deasserted.
- The FIPS-mode indication must be inactive.
- The RNG enable output must be inactive.
- The hardware entropy output must not assert acknowledge.
- The software entropy data output must return zero.

After reset, the module must remain disabled until explicitly enabled through configuration.

---

## 14. Summary of Required Behaviors

The entropy source core must:

- Collect raw entropy from the RNG interface when enabled.
- Support both FIPS and bypass operating modes.
- Perform continuous and window-based health tests.
- Provide an external health-test interface.
- Support firmware override and firmware entropy insertion.
- Condition raw entropy in FIPS mode and pack raw entropy in bypass mode.
- Store complete 384-bit seeds with FIPS-compliance flags.
- Deliver entropy to hardware and software output paths.
- Generate appropriate interrupts and alerts.
- Detect and report FIFO, counter, state-machine, and conditioner errors.
- Protect against invalid configuration and OTP-disabled operations.
- Provide full status and debug visibility through the register interface.
